Article Title: Ganga rises above 'highest flood mark' in Patna; several low-lying areas face inundation risk
Article Text:
A view of riverside ghats submerged amid the rise in Ganga River's water level, in Patna earlier this week

NEW DELHI: The Ganga breached the ‘highest flood mark’ at Patna’s Gandhi Ghat amid heavy rain in Bihar, with the river’s water level rising 10 cm in four hours on Saturday morning, according to an official bulletin.The river was flowing 1 cm above the highest flood level at 10 am, reaching 50.53 metres at Gandhi Ghat, the Water Resources Department (WRD) said.“The Ganga water level at Gandhi Ghat in Patna rose by 10 cm in the past four hours, reaching 50.53 cm, which is 1 cm above the highest flood level, at 10 am on Saturday,” the department said in its latest bulletin, as quoted by PTI.The situation could worsen further, with the WRD forecasting a continued rise in the river’s water level. “The forecast is that the Ganga water level at Gandhi Ghat is likely to rise further to 50.62 cm by 8 am on Sunday. People have been advised to exercise caution,” it said.The rising water has raised concerns over possible inundation in low-lying areas of Patna, with people being urged to remain cautious.Several districts across Bihar are already facing flood-like conditions as heavy rainfall in the state and neighbouring Nepal has pushed multiple rivers above their danger marks.The Ganga, Gandak, Kosi, Burhi Gandak, Bagmati, Punpun and Ghaghra are among the rivers flowing above danger levels.Chief minister Samrat Choudhary conducted an aerial survey of the affected areas on Friday and reviewed relief and rescue operations.He directed officials to identify affected families and ensure they receive relief on time. He also ordered continuous monitoring of vulnerable areas and the Ganga embankments between Buxar and Bhagalpur to prevent erosion and possible breaches.
Article Summary: The Ganga breached the ‘highest flood mark’ at Patna’s Gandhi Ghat amid heavy rain in Bihar. The river was flowing 1 cm above the highest flood level at 10 am, reaching 50.53 metres. The rising water has raised concerns over possible inundation in low-lying areas of Patna.

Article Title: 'Bound to breed contempt for law': SC judge Bhuyan on police action at Jantar Mantar protest
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan criticised police officers over the alleged assault on protesting students during the NEET agitation at Jantar Mantar and said that the detachment expected of officials appears to be disappearing.While speaking at the launch of former secretary (security) Yashovardhan Azad's book "Policing the Republic", Justice Bhuyan said that police must maintain their credibility because people seek their help when they feel wronged."All of us are dismayed when we see young officers of the Indian Police Service personally going and assaulting protesters and demonstrators. This is something very, very distressing to observe. The detachment expected of police officers somehow seems to be disappearing, and this is indeed a matter of grave concern," Justice Bhuyan said."For most common people, a policeman on the street wearing a whistle and a lathi represents the power and authority of the state. When they feel wronged, they seek the help of the police. It is, therefore, of utmost importance that the police force maintains its credibility.It can do so only by strictly adhering to the Constitution, by functioning as a truly professional force, acting impartially, displaying courage and acting with conviction, maintaining integrity and adhering to secular principles, thereby upholding the rule of law," he said.The Supreme Court judge further said that if government functionaries become lawbreakers, it is bound to breed contempt for the law and encourage lawlessness."If the functionaries of the government become lawbreakers, it is bound to breed contempt for the law and will encourage lawlessness. No civilised nation can permit that to happen. Does a citizen shed his fundamental right the moment a policeman arrests him?" Justice Bhuyan said.The alleged use of force by Delhi Police during the July 20 student protests at Jantar Mantar and the march towards Parliament has come under the Supreme Court's scrutiny, with the court constituting a high-level panel to examine complaints of excessive force.The panel, headed by former Supreme Court judge Justice R Subhash Reddy, will investigate allegations against Delhi Police and examine evidence including CCTV footage and videos of the protests.Among the allegations to be examined are the use of lathis, tear gas, pellet guns and electronic batons, as well as claims of targeted harassment and molestation of women protesters.
Article Summary: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan criticised police officers over the alleged assault on protesting students during the NEET agitation. He said that the detachment expected of officials appears to be disappearing. The alleged use of force by Delhi Police during the July 20 student protests at Jantar Mantar and the march towards Parliament has come under scrutiny.

NEW DELHI: Authorities on Saturday demolished a mosque located inside the district magistrate's office complex in Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur after a court upheld an earlier order declaring the structure illegal.Senior administrative officials, including the district magistrate and sub-divisional magistrate, reached the site as bulldozers began demolishing the structure. The collectorate complex was placed under heavy security, with Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC) personnel deployed and all gates shut as a precaution.Meanwhile, Samajawadi Party MP Iqra Hussain claimed that she was put under house arrest at her residence ahead of her scheduled visit to Saharanpur.Hasan said that a large police force was deployed outside her residence overnight and prevented her from leaving for Saharanpur."A large police force was deployed at my Kairana residence overnight, and I was placed under house arrest to prevent me from going to Saharanpur. I intended to visit Saharanpur to meet officials regarding the Collectorate mosque issue and to voice the concerns of the people of my constituency, but I was not even allowed to leave my home," Hasan told news agency ANI."In a democracy, public representatives are elected to raise the voice of the people. That voice cannot be suppressed by stopping me," she added.The demolition came a day after the district judge's court dismissed an appeal filed by the Muslim side challenging the City Magistrate's order.On September 4, the district judge's court, after hearing arguments from both sides and examining the evidence presented, upheld the city magistrate's order declaring the mosque illegal.The city magistrate's court had on July 17 ordered the demolition of the mosque and imposed compensation of around Rs 6.41 crore on the occupants over alleged illegal encroachment and misuse of government land.The case was initiated following a complaint by Vikas Tyagi, former provincial coordinator of Bajrang Dal, who alleged that the mosque had been built illegally inside the DM office complex, a sensitive government premises where confidential administrative work is carried out.The complaint also alleged that the premises were being used for commercial purposes apart from religious activities. According to the allegations, a post office was operating from the site and some rooms had been rented out to outsiders, with the mosque committee allegedly collecting monthly rent.The district administration had argued that the alleged encroachment and commercial use of the premises raised security concerns, particularly given the sensitive nature of government operations conducted there.The development comes amid similar administrative action against alleged illegal religious structures in various parts of Uttar Pradesh.
Article Summary: Authorities on Saturday demolished a mosque located inside the district magistrate's office complex in Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur. A court upheld an earlier order declaring the structure illegal. Samajawadi Party MP Iqra Hussain claimed that she was put under house arrest at her residence ahead of her scheduled visit.

Article Title: 'Exceptionally rare': All 3 hydraulic systems of Air India Phuket-Delhi flight failed together
Article Text:
The hydraulic failure itself, the more immediate cause of the injuries onboard, unfolded within a five-second window. VT-EXO, an eight-year-old A320neo carrying 145 people, had just been cleared to climb from FL340 to FL360 after entering Kolkata Flight Information Region.

‘Triple hydraulic failure close to unthinkable’

MUMBAI: Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau's preliminary report has confirmed what pilots and engineers call an exceptionally rare event, the near-simultaneous loss of all three hydraulic systems on the A320neo aircraft at 36,000 feet. Hydraulic systems are the fluid-pressure circuits that physically move an aircraft's wing and tail surfaces. The green, blue and yellow systems dropped out within seconds of each other, triggering an autopilot disengagement, a stall warning and a brief altitude upset that injured 24 flyers.The accident occurred when the eight-year-old A320neo (VT-EXO) carrying 145 people had just been cleared to climb from 34,000 feet to 36,000 feet after entering the airspace controlled by Kolkata ATC. At 9:32:43am IST, within four seconds the flight control system detected loss of all the three hydraulic systems.In the next few seconds, the autopilot disengaged, a continuous repetitive chime sounded, and the stall warning triggered for two seconds. “The aircraft encountered altitude upset. Initially, it gained 372 ft and fell by 292 ft from its assigned 36,000 feet flight level during the event,” the report said.It did not give information on the cause of the triple hydraulic failure, nor did it put forth any safety recommendations for the A320 aircraft type. It said the investigation is in progress and hydraulic components, fluid samples and recorder data have been collected and are still being analysed.The critical information on the probable cause and contributory factors is likely to be released in the final report, expected to be published on or before Aug 4, 2027.In simple terms, hydraulic pressure is what physically moves an aircraft’s control surfaces, the ailerons on the wings that make it roll, the elevators on the tail that make it pitch up or down, and the rudder that makes it yaw left or right. Pilots move the stick and pedals, but it is hydraulic power that pushes the actual surfaces. An A320 carries three independent hydraulic circuits so that losing one, or even two, still leaves enough pressure to fly and manoeuvre the aircraft normally.“Losing all three at once is considered close to unthinkable, because the A320 has a triple-redundant hydraulic design which ensures no combination of failures can disable flight controls entirely. It is the kind of failure engineers cite alongside a handful of decades-old incidents involving other aircraft types, none of them an A320,” said a senior aircraft maintenance engineer. The notable total hydraulic loss events that occurred globally are the 1985 JAL 123 (Boeing 747), the 1989 United Airlines DC-10, and a DHL A300 that was hit by a missile over Baghdad in 2003.Following the triple hydraulic failure, the co-pilot, who was flying the aircraft, responded first to the upset before the captain took over the controls. Recovery was swift, the blue system came back within seconds, followed shortly by yellow and green, restoring normal flight control surfaces, the report said.
Article Summary: The accident occurred when the eight-year-old A320neo (VT-EXO) carrying 145 people had just been cleared to climb to 36,000 feet. The green, blue and yellow systems dropped out within seconds of each other, triggering an autopilot disengagement, a stall warning and a brief altitude upset.

Article Title: Punjab Police detains FBI-wanted fugitive accused of defrauding US government of $600,000
Article Text:
Jalandhar Police detains US-wanted fugitive Manjit Singh Bedi linked to SNAP fraud case

NEW DELHI: Jalandhar Commissionerate Police detained Manjit Singh Bedi, a fugitive wanted in the US in connection with an alleged SNAP benefits fraud case, Punjab Director General of Police Gaurav Yadav said on Friday.Bedi was reportedly placed on the US Most-Wanted Fraudsters list over allegations of defrauding the US government of more than $600,000 through a scheme involving Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits. According to the Punjab DGP, Bedi allegedly fled to India via Canada in April 2026 to evade US law enforcement."In a major breakthrough, Jalandhar Commissionerate Police apprehends Manjit Singh Bedi, a wanted fugitive linked to a US-based benefits fraud case. Bedi was reportedly placed on the US Most-Wanted Fraudsters list in connection with a SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) benefits fraud case in the #USA and had allegedly fled to #India via #Canada in April 2026 to evade the law," the DGP posted on X.The FBI had earlier alleged that Bedi, an India-born naturalised US citizen, operated Asian Grocery Store in Tacoma, Washington, where he used customers' Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) cards to process transactions without providing food.He allegedly gave SNAP participants cash instead and kept half of the proceeds.“Instead of selling participants food, Bedi is alleged to have swiped their cards and given them cash,” the FBI said in its wanted notice.Bedi was indicted in the US on charges of wire fraud and SNAP benefits fraud. He was initially allowed to appear in court without being arrested and was ordered to surrender his passport and remain in Washington state, but the FBI said he later fled to Canada and then India.A federal arrest warrant was issued against him on May 21, 2026, in the US District Court for the Western District of Washington after he allegedly violated the conditions of his supervision. The FBI had offered a reward of up to $150,000 for information leading to his arrest and conviction.The Punjab DGP said the police force remains committed to tracking fugitives and tackling transnational organised crime.“Punjab Police remains relentless in tracking down fugitives and dismantling transnational organised crime networks, ensuring that no one can evade justice by crossing borders,” he said.In a separate development earlier on Friday, the State Special Operation Cell (SSOC) Amritsar and Counter Intelligence Amritsar arrested six people in two operations targeting alleged weapons and narcotics smuggling modules.Police recovered 2.9 kg of heroin, eight high-end pistols and six live cartridges, besides impounding a car and a motorcycle allegedly used in the smuggling activities.Preliminary investigation indicated that the accused were allegedly involved in cross-border smuggling and received weapons and narcotics consignments through drones for distribution among criminal elements in Punjab, the DGP said. Further investigation is underway to establish the network's forward and backward linkages.
Article Summary: Jalandhar Commissionerate Police detained Manjit Singh Bedi, a fugitive wanted in the US in connection with an alleged SNAP benefits fraud case. Bedi was reportedly placed on the US Most-Wanted Fraudsters list over allegations of defrauding the US government of more than $600,000. According to the Punjab DGP, Bedi allegedly fled to India via Canada in April 2026.

Article Title: 'Cracked skull' wasn't all: In eye of storm, 'influencer' Swatantra Bhardwaj
Article Text:
Swatantra Bhardwaj, 22, was detained in Uttar Pradesh's Bulandshahr district.

A provocative online presence

The hunt for Bhardwaj

(With inputs from PTI)

Poll Vote & Share your view Is the government doing enough to hold influencers accountable for their actions online? Yes, they are taking action No, they need to do more 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





NEW DELHI: Long before the viral video in which he boasted about assaulting a Jantar Mantar protester’s father, 'influencer' Swatantra Bhardwaj had built a sizeable following through provocative posts, political associations and incendiary remarks.Bhardwaj, 22, was detained in Uttar Pradesh's Bulandshahr district on Friday, hours after Delhi Police assured protesters from the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) that he would be arrested within 72 hours.Bhardwaj is accused of assaulting the father of student activist Nishu Azad during a protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi on July 20.His detention came after a clip from an interview went viral in which Bhardwaj is heard claiming that he had "cracked the skull" of the father."Do you know which section this crime attracts? Section 307. He needed 60 stitches. The man was being taken away in an ambulance in serious condition. His daughter was standing outside the police station and saying that she would die by suicide if her father didn't get justice."But I was not even jailed. The world should know this. I was out and about through the night," Bhardwaj is heard saying in the video.He then named several political leaders while explaining why, according to him, he had little reason to fear arrest."I have the blessings of Hanuman upon me. And secondly, Kapil Mishra is my elder brother. They say Kapil Mishra called and I was released. Chirag Paswan is my elder brother. How many leaders do you know? Do you know Modi ji? Modi ji is also my elder brother. I have everyone's support," he claimed.There is, however, no evidence to establish that any of the political leaders named by Bhardwaj intervened on his behalf in the case.The viral clip also brought renewed attention to Bhardwaj's older social media posts and videos.According to news agency PTI, his Facebook page, which has around 327,000 followers, contains posts focused on cow protection, attacks on Muslims and critics of the government, as well as photographs appearing to show his proximity to political figures and official events.Some older videos circulating on social media purportedly show him making inflammatory remarks about Muslims and government critics. In others, he boasts about his political connections and claims he does not fear arrest.His online presence suggests that the persona seen in the viral clip was not an isolated episode, but part of a broader public image he had cultivated over time.On Thursday, a day before his detention, Bhardwaj shared a screenshot showing his name among the trends on X, captioning it, "Love you all Virodhi".He also posted a photograph on Instagram showing a 'kada' on his wrist with the caption "Feel the power!". The post appeared to reference a Delhi Police statement that Kumar had been injured by a 'kada' and "not by any weapon".His social media accounts also featured photographs with political leaders, including Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, Delhi minister Kapil Mishra and Union minister Chirag Paswan.Paswan said on Friday that Bhardwaj had misused his name and the names of other leaders.The Union minister for food processing industries said he had lodged a complaint against Bhardwaj and demanded action against him."No action despite the accused admitting to an attack that could have been fatal sets a bad example; I take responsibility for ensuring justice for the family," Paswan said.Bhardwaj's accounts also included what appeared to be AI-generated images of him with women wearing burqas or hijabs.One particularly violent image, posted on 22 May, showed Bhardwaj holding the bloodied chin of a man. The accompanying text referred to "Mughal" and included the words "aa gaya swad".His Instagram account, which had around 184,000 followers, was deactivated on Friday. He also has a verified account on X with more than 6,400 followers.The viral video intensified demands for action against Bhardwaj, with protesters raising the issue during the CJP demonstration in Delhi on Friday.Police subsequently deployed several teams to trace him.According to police officials, Bhardwaj had travelled to Bulandshahr and was staying in Naithla village. He allegedly fled the village on a motorcycle towards Khurja before a police team could apprehend him.He was wearing a helmet, apparently in an attempt to conceal his identity, police said.Local residents told TOI that Bhardwaj had arrived in Bulandshahr early on Friday, allegedly to evade arrest, and had taken shelter at the home of a local family.While there, he interacted with some journalists and reportedly repeated his claims about the alleged assault during the CJP protest.Bhardwaj was staying at the house of Harishankar Sharma, a Naithla resident who works as a cab driver in the Delhi-NCR region.Sharma said he had met Bhardwaj during an earlier journey.“Bhardwaj called me and said he wanted to come to my house to meet me. He arrived early in the morning along with another man. Initially, I did not suspect anything. But when media persons started arriving at my village, I sensed something was wrong,” Sharma said.Sharma said Bhardwaj later asked to borrow his motorcycle, saying he would return “within five minutes”.“Then I came to know that Delhi Police had detained him. It was only after that I learnt that he was wanted in a criminal case in the national capital. I still do not know much about the case,” Sharma said.The detention came after CJP representatives said Delhi Police had assured them that Bhardwaj “will be arrested within 72 hours”.The case has since drawn attention not only to the alleged assault but also to the online persona Bhardwaj had built through provocative posts, political associations and claims of influence.
Article Summary: Swatantra Bhardwaj, 22, was detained in Uttar Pradesh's Bulandshahr district on Friday. He is accused of assaulting the father of student activist Nishu Azad during a protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi on July 20. His detention came after a clip from an interview went viral in which he claimed he had "cracked the skull" of the father.

Article Title: RSS says of critics of Mohan Bhagwat’s UK trip: ‘Let them speak, we’re open to dialogue’
Article Text:
RSS spokesman Sunil Ambekar in London for Mohan Bhagwat visit

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

LONDON: The RSS shrugged off criticism by civil groups of its chief Dr Mohan Bhagwat’s UK trip, saying in a democracy differences of opinions are expected and “should not be taken as a shock”.The RSS head arrived in London on Sept 2 on the final leg of his three-city outreach RSS centenary tour, having just visited New York and Toronto on a “dialogue mission.”Hindus for Human Rights UK and several other campaign groups wrote an open letter to London mayor Sadiq Khan asking him to condemn the visit, pointing out New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani had done that.Labour PIO MP Nadia Whittome tabled a written parliamentary question asking the home office whether “the visit engages the commitment to block hate preachers and extremists from entering the UK”.“We are here for peace, integration and oneness and we are open for dialogue with everyone. In a democracy, it is very normal to raise different voices. We are engaging with those who wish to dialogue with us,” RSS head of media Sunil Ambekar said at a press briefing on Friday.“We are here to communicate what we are and how we think. We are very much open. We have nothing to hide. We expect a debate and exchange of thoughts. Let them speak.”On allegations the RSS was behind the 2022 Leicester riots, Ambekar said this was a “UK domestic issue”. “There is no question… RSS was not involved. Already people are finding out their legal options. Hindus are a peace-loving community.”He said there are a lot of “misconceptions” in the West. “Bharat is not a nation state political concept — it is a cultural concept. Hindutva is not like any religion — it’s a concept where there will be respect for all religious practices. That is Hindutva, and that is Bharat, so I think the trip will help to clear the ideas,” he said.A spokesperson for the London mayor said the mayor “does not have the power” to ban people from speaking. “London is proud to celebrate our diversity and intolerance has no place in our great city,” the spokesperson said.
Article Summary: Mohan Bhagwat arrived in London on Sept 2 on the final leg of his three-city outreach RSS centenary tour. Civil groups wrote an open letter to London mayor Sadiq Khan asking him to condemn the visit. “In a democracy, it is very normal to raise different voices,” RSS head of media Sunil Ambekar said at a press briefing on Friday.

SRINAGAR: Security forces Friday gunned down a terrorist during an anti-terror operation deep inside a forest area in J&K’s Budgam district, about 60km from Srinagar, the Army stated.Based on intelligence inputs, a joint team of the Army, J&K Police and CRPF launched a search operation in Budgam’s Ashdar Gali area, the Army’s Srinagar-based Chinar Corps stated in an X post.Holed-up ultras opened fire at the search party, triggering a fierce gunfight in which one terrorist was shot dead. Article Title: Army rescues minor from being swept away towards Pak
Article Text:
Army personnel Friday rescued a minor girl from being swept away

JAMMU: Alert Army personnel Friday rescued a minor girl from being swept away towards Pakistan by the strong currents of a seasonal rivulet in J&K’s Poonch district.“Around 1.10pm, troops of Army’s 30 Punjab Regiment manning a forward post spotted the girl, aged around 14-15 years, being washed away in the strong currents of the seasonal Mendhar nullah from Balnoi and along the Roshni-Mandi belt towards Pakistan,” an official said.“Soldiers jumped into the water and pulled her out in an unconscious condition at Katra post. She was rushed to Mankote primary health centre,” the official said. Local police, medical authorities, and the village head of the area were also present.Officials said the health of the teen, a resident of Balnoi in Poonch district, had since stabilised and her family members were informed about her condition.
Article Summary: Army personnel Friday rescued a minor girl from being swept away towards Pakistan by the strong currents of a seasonal rivulet in J&K’s Poonch district. “Soldiers jumped into the water and pulled her out in an unconscious condition at Katra post. She was rushed to Mankote primary health centre,” an official said.

Article Title: Possession of separatist literature no ground for PSA detention, rules J&K HC
Article Text:
Mere possession of books with “dispiriting titles” does not make a person a criminal the Jammu & Kashmir high court said

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: Mere possession of books with “dispiriting titles” does not make a person a criminal, the Jammu & Kashmir high court said, quashing an order for preventive detention of a man under the Public Safety Act (PSA) on charges of keeping and authoring books promoting separatist ideology.A single bench of Justice Moksha Khajuria Kazmi Thursday also observed that the PSA detention order passed by Kupwara district magistrate against the petitioner, Shafat Maqbool Wani, wrongly attributed to him the authorship of alleged anti-national literature seized from his house.Being a scholar, the petitioner could be expected to possess a variety of literary material, the court said, directing police to release Wani forthwith.Police claimed to have seized books with what they alleged were incriminating titles — ‘Construction of an Islamic Order in Hindutva Reimagination’ and ‘The Saffronization of occupied Kashmir, Demystifing Hindutva Settlers, Colonial Designers’ —from Wani’s house. They also attributed the authorship of the books to Wani.The court said the assertion that the detainee had inculcated a separatist ideology since his childhood as his father has been an ex-militant was “delusory”.“...The preventive detention, ordered so conveniently on such imaginary belief, is nothing but an unmindful exercise of power,” it observed.Justice Kazmi noted that the respondents had not shown any subversive activity against the petitioner that compelled them to take recourse to preventive detention.The HC ruling assumes significance as the home department banned the publication and circulation of 25 books on Kashmir, saying they promoted a “false narrative” and “secessionism”, on Aug 5, 2025, the sixth anniversary of abrogation of Article 370.The books include ‘Azadi’ by Arundhati Roy, ‘Kashmir: The Case for Freedom’, a collection of essays by Tariq Ali, Pankaj Mishra and others; ‘Confronting Terrorism’, also a collection of essays, edited by Maroof Raza; and ‘In Search of a Future’ by journalist and author David Devadas.The Kupwara DM ordered Wani’s detention under PSA on Sept 13, 2025, to prevent him from indulging in activities “detrimental to the security of the State”. The grounds cited included invitations he had received to attend some international conferences. The detention order came the same day he was granted bail by a Jammu NIA court in a UAPA case registered at Handwara police station.
Article Summary: Jammu & Kashmir high court quashes order for preventive detention of a man under the Public Safety Act (PSA) Shafat Maqbool Wani was accused of keeping and authoring books promoting separatist ideology. Police claimed to have seized books with what they alleged were incriminating titles.

Article Title: 'No one could erase Sanatan Dharma': Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi Adityanath celebrates Janmashtami in Mathura
Article Text:
Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi Adityanath celebrates Janmashtami in Mathura

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MATHURA: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath offered prayers at the historic Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Temple on Friday, participating in the Janmashtami celebrations and greeting devotees by showering flower petals.Addressing the occasion in Mathura, Adityanath underscored the timeless significance of Lord Krishna's teachings, asserting that teachings from millennia ago continue to guide society. The Uttar Pradesh CM noted that forces seeking to disrupt national unity, integrity, or faith will inevitably face the consequences outlined in sacred texts.He said, "The proclamations made by Lord Krishna over 5000 years ago remain just as relevant today. Its relevance is upheld by the principle of 'Paritranaya Sadhunam Vinashaya cha Dushkritam'; wherever the forces of goodness exist, they will be protected under all circumstances. However, regarding anti-national and anti-social forces that raise their heads to sow discord in society and attempt to harm India's unity, integrity, or faith, Lord Krishna had declared 5,000 years ago what their fate would be. "Highlighting the resilience of India's cultural heritage, the Chief Minister remarked that despite numerous historical invasions and attempts to suppress indigenous faiths, Sanatan Dharma has remained enduringly vibrant.He stated that those who dared to challenge or attempt to erase the tradition have vanished into oblivion."There were numerous invasions, and many attempted to impose their own faiths upon India, yet no one could erase the Sanatan Dharma. Those who had the audacity to try and obliterate the Sanatan Dharma were themselves reduced to dust and faded into oblivion. However, not only in Braj-bhoomi but across all of India, the memory of Shri Krishna and Radha Rserves as an inspiration for us today and fosters an atmosphere of enthusiasm and progress for future generations," Yogi Adityanath said.Mathura, the birthplace of Lord Krishna, lit up in colourful illuminations as the city celebrates Janmashtami, with temples and religious sites decorated.Meanwhile, on Friday, Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended greetings to the people on the occasion of Janmashtami, invoking Lord Krishna's teachings on selfless action and their enduring relevance.In a post on X, PM Modi wrote, "Heartfelt Janmashtami greetings to all of you. In the divine messages of Lord Shri Krishna lies the profound inspiration for selfless action, which has continuously guided humanity. May this sacred occasion, dedicated to his devotion and worship, infuse positive energy and strength into everyone's life-that is my heartfelt wish. Jai Shri Krishna!"Krishna Janmashtami, also known simply as Janmashtami or Gokulashtami, is an annual Hindu festival that celebrates the birth of Krishna, the eighth avatar of Vishnu. It is observed according to the Hindu luni-solar calendar, on the eighth day (Ashtami) of the Krishna Paksha (dark fortnight) in the month of Bhadrapada, which overlaps with August and September of the Gregorian calendar.Meanwhile, devotees across the country are celebrating Janmashtami with religious fervour, gathering at temples for Mangla Aarti and special prayers to mark the birth of Lord Krishna.In Delhi, devotees gathered in large numbers at ISKCON temples in East of Kailash and Dwarka Sector 13 to participate in the Mangla Aarti held on the occasion of Janmashtami. Devotees joined the prayers and celebrated the festival at the temples.At the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Temple in Mathura, devotees took part in Mangala Aarti and special prayers as celebrations continued at the birthplace of Lord Krishna. People also danced and expressed their devotion to Lord Krishna.Mathura witnessed a particularly devotional atmosphere as devotees gathered at the temples across the city to participate in the religious ceremonies marking Janmashtami. The celebrations included prayers and rituals conducted at the temple, with devotees joining in the festivities.Religious celebrations and large gatherings have brought a festive atmosphere across the country as devotees come together to celebrate Janmashtami.
Article Summary: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath offered prayers at the historic Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Temple in Mathura. He underscored the timeless significance of Lord Krishna's teachings, asserting that teachings from millennia ago continue to guide society. Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended greetings to the people on the occasion.

NEW DELHI: The West Bengal fire department has ordered the evacuation of the basement, sixth and seventh floors of a high-rise building in central Kolkata that houses TMC leader Abhishek Banerjee 's office, citing a "lack of fire safety measures", an official said on Friday.The order came a day after Banerjee's Camac Street office was ransacked, with the TMC blaming BJP-linked men for the attack. CJP’s student campaign

Meeting ahead of UP polls

Article Title: Blinkit's Mangaluru storage sealed after customer finds worm inside egg

MANGALURU: Food safety officials in Karnataka inspected a Blinkit online retail facility in Mangaluru after a consumer alleged that a worm was found inside an egg purchased through the quick-commerce platform.The complaint was reportedly submitted to Health Minister U T Khader, following which officials inspected the facility operating from Falnir Square in the city's Falnir area.During the inspection, officials found packets containing broken eggs and directed the facility staff to immediately remove and dispose of the affected stock, according to an official release.As a precautionary measure, the storage room was temporarily closed and sealed to allow thorough cleaning and sanitisation of the food storage area.The Food Safety Department said it would issue a notice to the establishment seeking an explanation over the incident. Further action will be decided based on the inspection findings and the response submitted by the facility management.The inspection comes amid increased scrutiny of food safety and hygiene standards in Karnataka. In a separate action, the Department of Food Safety and Drug Administration recently closed and seized a kitchen at Chairman's Club in Sahakaranagar's Dollars Colony area of Bengaluru after officials found multiple alleged violations during a special inspection drive conducted on September 3.Officials said around 40 kg of expired chilli was found and seized during the inspection. The department also flagged improper labelling of certain food products, unhygienic conditions in food preparation and storage areas, alleged use or storage of unauthorised artificial colours, lapses in food handling and storage practices, and the storage of vegetarian and non-vegetarian food products together.The department said it would continue inspections and take legal action against food businesses found violating food safety and hygiene norms.
Article Summary: Food safety officials in Karnataka inspected a Blinkit facility in Mangaluru. A consumer alleged that a worm was found inside an egg purchased through the quick-commerce platform. The complaint was reportedly submitted to Health Minister U T Khader. During the inspection, officials found packets containing broken eggs.

NAMAKKAL: Three young sisters and their 11-year-old cousin riding on a moped died after a private college bus collided with their vehicle at Elachipalayam near Tiruchengode in Namakkal district on Thursday.The deceased were identified as S Kalaichelvi, 19, a second-year student at a government college; her sisters Nivedha, 15, a Class XI student, and Dhanushree, 11, a Class VII student; and their cousin R Abinaya, 11, a Class VI student. Article Title: ‘Asked our community, then thrashed us again’: Journalists 'assaulted' at Delhi's Saket police station, cops deny
Article Text:
Two women YouTubers claim Delhi Police assaulted them after detention at Saket police station





NEW DELHI: Two women journalists and YouTubers alleged that they were detained and assaulted by Delhi Police personnel after attempting to question chief minister Rekha Gupta at an event in south Delhi on Thursday. Police denied the allegations, describing them as “factually incorrect” and “misleading”.According to the women, they had gone to cover the inauguration of a new wing at Max Hospital in Saket, attended by Union home minister Amit Shah and the Delhi chief minister. One of them alleged in a video circulated on social media that they were stopped while trying to question Gupta and taken to Saket police station.“We wanted to question the Delhi chief minister. But we were detained and brought to Saket Police Station. The police teams took us to a room, where they assaulted us brutally. They asked which community we belonged to and thrashed us again,” the journalist alleged.The women claimed they were taken to a room inside the police station, where they were assaulted and abused. They alleged that both sustained injuries during the incident. Videos showing the women displaying injury marks on different parts of their bodies were also circulated on social media, though the allegations could not be independently verified.Delhi Police rejected the accusations and gave a different account of the events, saying the women had obstructed a designated VVIP security route by parking their scooter near the venue.A senior police officer said the women were not carrying identity cards and were repeatedly asked to move their vehicle after being informed about the security arrangements. Police further alleged that they created a ruckus and manhandled a pregnant police officer.The women were subsequently taken to Saket police station for enquiry, police said, adding that they were free to leave within five to 10 minutes of reaching the station and were not restrained.“Nobody was holding their hands or preventing them from leaving, but they chose not to go,” an officer said.Deputy Commissioner of Police (South) Anant Mittal described claims that the women were assaulted for attempting to question the chief minister as “totally false, misleading and baseless” and urged people not to circulate unverified information.Meanwhile, several journalists’ organisations condemned the alleged assault and demanded a free and fair investigation.The Press Club of India, Indian Women’s Press Corps, Delhi Union of Journalists, Press Association and Kerala Union of Working Journalists, in a joint statement, alleged that the two freelance journalists were manhandled near the venue before being taken to Saket police station and assaulted there.The organisations demanded action against those responsible and urged Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar to order a fair probe. They also appealed to the Press Council of India to take suo motu cognisance of the matter.The Aam Aadmi Party also targeted the BJP-led Delhi government, with party leader Saurabh Bharadwaj alleging that the journalists were assaulted for asking questions of the chief minister.Delhi Police, however, maintained that the allegations were baseless and that the women were taken to the police station after they allegedly refused to comply with security instructions on the designated VVIP route.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Two women journalists and YouTubers claim Delhi Police assaulted them after detention at Saket police station. Police deny the allegations, describing them as “factually incorrect’ and “misleading’ Delhi Police said the women had obstructed a designated VVIP security route by parking their scooter near the venue.

Article Title: Gogi 2.0? Ankit Balyan murder brings gang back on Delhi Police radar
Article Text:
Haryanvi singer and Youtube Ankit Balyan

Delhi's underworld overhaul





NEW DELHI: The echo of gunfire outside a gym in UP’s Shamli on Aug 26 did more than just silence 27-year-old Haryanvi singer and YouTuber Ankit Balyan. It marked the revival of Delhi’s most feared Gogi gang, suggesting the syndicate remains active five years after kingpin Jitender Maan alias Gogi’s assassination in a crowded Rohini courtroom.Despite its core leadership — Rohit Moi, Deepak Boxer , Dinesh Karala, Yogesh Tunda and Deepak Teetar — in Tihar, the gang has managed to come out of the shadows with Balyan’s killing, ringing alarm bells in Delhi, with cops keeping a cautious watch on the developments. Specialised units have been roped in for a manhunt for the absconding shooters in the Balyan case amid fears they can strike in the city next, engage in extortion bids and kill rivals, according to sources.The gang’s resurgence is particularly alarming given that it has suffered massive setbacks. Besides the kingpin’s killing, the other gang members have been regularly arrested in Delhi and Haryana in the past two-three years. The rival Tajpuria gang dealt further blows with two back-to-back killings of Gogi’s henchmen earlier this year in outer Delhi. But the cartel’s hierarchy seems to have mutated rather than collapsed.So, how did the gang manage a comeback? Investigators suspect low-rung foot soldiers on bail and foreign-based handlers like Rahul alias Bholu Shahpuria helped the gang emerge from the shadows again. Also, the gang’s incarcerated bigwigs still seem to be active while in jail. A critical catalyst for the renewed aggression seems to be a strategic underworld alliance with the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, forged years ago by Jitender Gogi himself.Supported by Lawrence’s overarching umbrella, the gang now relies on an expendable army of low-rung foot soldiers who are being allegedly recruited through Instagram and promised an “out of country” card after successful completion of tasks. The two absconding shooters in the Balyan case, it is suspected, may have fled abroad too. These street-level operatives are allegedly being coordinated by fugitive entities operating safely from foreign soil. Figures like Bholu Shahpuria, based in Canada, have stepped in to manage logistics.What has alarmed Delhi cops further is the apparent trigger in Balyan’s killing, which underscores the syndicate’s obsession with retribution. Balyan was allegedly a target for a music video featuring the lyrics “Bhari court me goli maarenge meri jaan”, with visual references to shooters dressed as lawyers. “The Gogi gang perceived the track as a direct insult mocking Gogi’s 2021 courtroom killing. The ‘insult’ was further magnified by the fact that Balyan shared the same local roots as Gogi’s rival, Tillu Tajpuria,” said an investigator.For years, Delhi witnessed a slew of killings — at least 36 murders in the past 15 years — in the gang war between Gogi and Tajpuria. Retired officials said this rivalry began one and a half decades ago as a college election dispute between childhood friends Gogi and Tajpuria morphed into a turf war.After Gogi’s killing, Deepak Boxer took the reins and ran the gang from Mexico, but he was tracked down and brought back after a complex operation by FBI and Delhi Police in April 2023.The Gogi gang extracted vengeance a month later when incarcerated loyalists — led by Yogesh Tunda and Deepak Titar — cornered Tillu Tajpuria inside Tihar Jail’s courtyard and stabbed him over 100 times with makeshift shivs.
Article Summary: Ankit Balyan's killing marks revival of Delhi's most feared Gogi gang. Specialised units have been roped in for a manhunt for the absconding shooters. Investigators suspect low-rung foot soldiers on bail and foreign-based handlers helped gang emerge from shadows.
