Article Title: 1,000 Vidya Bharati schools in Bengal within a year, says CM Suvendu Adhikari
Article Text:
West Bengal's Chief Minister urged Vidya Bharati to establish one thousand new schools.

By: Subhajoy Roy

TOI





KOLKATA: Every district, municipality and panchayat in the state should host a school by Vidya Bharati, the education wing of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), CM Suvendu Adhikari said on Thursday and set a target of establishing at least 1,000 such institutions in Bengal within the next year.The CM invited the Vidya Bharati leadership to meet the entire education department at the state secretariat and added that Vidya Bharati must take responsibility for imparting nationalistic learning. Adhikari was speaking at an event to mark the 74th year of Vidya Bharati at Ramakrishna Mission Institute of Culture in Golpark.Bengal currently has 313 Vidya Bharati schools. Nationally, Vidya Bharati runs over 12,000 schools and 10,000 Bal Sanskar Kendras.Adhikari also signalled the merger of state’s four education departments — school education, higher education, technical and minority education — to establish a single department. “Our belief is to have a single education department. There will be no madrassa education department and others. You keep watching,” he said and added that the previous govt had polluted the state’s education environment and Vidya Bharati’s “help will be needed to come out of this”.He insisted Vidya Bharati should set up more schools in Murshidabad and South 24 Parganas, where “more anti-national activities take place”.Anand Rao, an official of Vidya Bharati, toldtheir schools train students in “bharatiyatwa (Indianness)” as well as puja rituals. “There are 313 schools in Bengal. Some are till class 5 and some till classes 8, 10 and 12,” he said. There are also 150 Sanskar Kendras where students learn puja rituals and about Indian culture and tradition.The website of Vidya Bharati Akhil Bhartiya Shiksha Sansthan says its vision is “to develop a national system of education which would help build a younger generation which is committed to Hindutva and infused with patriotic fervour”.The CM accused the previous Trinamool govt of deliberately and strategically twisting the Bengali syllabus in schools to divide Bengali-speaking people.“Mother was referred to as ‘amma’ and not ‘ma’. Similarly, the sky was referred to as ‘asman’ and not ‘akash’. Bengali language was distorted in a planned manner. The syllabus was created in such a way that Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar’s or Swami Vivekananda’s lessons remained neglected. Division was created in the minds of children through such distortion of language,” he alleged.Adhikari said Syama Prasad Mookerjee’s call of ‘ek desh, ek bidhan, ek nishan, ek pradhan’ would apply to education as well. “We will not allow an arrangement where the higher education department will look after all universities while another department will look after Aliah University,” he said. Aliah University is managed by Bengal govt’s minority affairs department.“I felicitated the board toppers. Later the minority affairs department sent a separate file for felicitating 27 Muslim students. I asked why? Students do not have religion. I have already felicitated 20 students and they include Muslims, Jaina, Buddhists,” he said.Adhikari added that he had seen a video where a student, who wore a tilak on his head, was forced to wipe it off in school. He did not name the school. He added that the govt knew how to overcome opposition to singing Vande Mataram in schools. “Some were saying they will not sing it. I said we will stop funds. Then they agreed to sing. Still they were not moving their lips. I told the education secretary that they will have to sing ‘tomari murti gori mandir e mandir e’ (we build your idols in temples),” he said.The CM added that he had also requested Union defence minister Rajnath Singh to establish more Sainik schools in the state. “Rajnath ji was in Kolkata recently. I said give Bengal more Sainik schools. I told him that I will write to you to introduce NCC in each school. I have already sent the letters. Vidya Bharati can help with these. We will work together,” he added.
Article Summary: Bengal currently has 313 Vidya Bharati schools. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari set a target of establishing at least 1,000 such institutions in Bengal within the next year. He also signalled the merger of state’s four education departments.

Article Title: Fire breaks out at Maharashtra's Asian Hospital; over 50 patients, including 9 infants rescued
Article Text:
Fire erupted at Asian Hospital in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar early Friday morning





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: A major fire broke out at Asian Hospital in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar around 2.30 am on Friday, triggering panic among patients, relatives and hospital staff.According to Fire Brigade officials, around 58 patients were admitted to the hospital when the blaze broke out, including nine newborns in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU). All patients were safely evacuated in a swift operation.No patient or hospital staff member was injured, officials said.Thick smoke engulfed parts of the building, prompting hospital staff to raise the alarm and alert the Fire Brigade. Three fire tenders were rushed to the spot, and firefighters began efforts to bring the blaze under control.The incident caused panic among relatives, with several of them rushing to the hospital after learning about the fire. Police personnel also reached the spot and cordoned off the area.The exact cause of the fire was not immediately known, though a short circuit is suspected to have triggered the blaze.
Article Summary: Fire broke out at Asian Hospital in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar around 2.30 am on Friday. Around 58 patients were admitted to the hospital when the blaze broke out, including nine newborns in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) All patients were safely evacuated in a swift operation.

Article Title: Watch: Stray dogs foil drunk boy’s bid to sexually assault mentally ill woman in Coimbatore
Article Text:
Stray dogs intervened to save a mentally ill woman from an alleged assault

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your opinion on the role of stray dogs in the community after this incident? They are protective and should be valued. They might pose a risk to safety. They should be removed from the area. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





COIMBATORE: Stray dogs saved a mentally ill woman from a sexual assault attempt by a drunk 17-year-old boy on the outskirts of Coimbatore in the early hours of Thursday.The incident occurred near NGGO Colony in Thudiyalur around 2am. Police, who were checking CCTV footage to investigate a complaint regarding an arson attempt on a petty shop in the area, stumbled upon the visuals of the teenager’s attempt to sexually assault the woman.According to police sources, the woman was sitting before her relative’s house near a railway overbridge when the minor boy approached her under the influence of alcohol.The CCTV footage showed two stray dogs barking persistently at the suspect as he approached the victim. When the suspect tried to overpower and assault the woman, she raised an alarm. Immediately, one of the dogs came to her rescue and bit him on his legs a few times. Overwhelmed by the dog attack, the suspect fled the scene. The dog chased him away.Based on the visual evidence from the footage, the Thudiyalur police registered a case and arrested the boy on Friday. He was produced before the Juvenile Justice Board and lodged in an observation home in the city.A police officer said the boy from Ganesh Nagar was addicted to alcohol and was doing notorious activities under the influence of liquor.
Article Summary: Stray dogs saved a mentally ill woman from a sexual assault attempt by a drunk 17-year-old boy on the outskirts of Coimbatore in the early hours of Thursday. The incident occurred near NGGO Colony in Thudiyalur around 2am. The CCTV footage showed two stray dogs barking persistently at the suspect as he approached the victim.

Article Title: Not given FIR copy, says ex-bureaucrat Ashish Joshi; no need at this stage, say cops
Article Text:
Ex-bureaucrat Ashish Joshi





NEW DELHI: Former bureaucrat Ashish Joshi , who was questioned by Delhi Police 's special cell for several hours Wednesday, said he and his lawyers were yet to be pro-vided with a copy of the FIR against him.Speaking to TOI, Joshi, a 1992-batch officer of the Indian Post and Telecommunication Accounts and Finance Service, said he went to Delhi Police headquarters Thursday with a letter from his lawyers asking that he be provided with a copy of the FIR against him. The FIR has been registered under section 192 of Bharatiya Nyay Sanhita, which relates to "wantonly giving provocation with intent to cause riot".Joshi said he was approached by two Delhi Police officers as he was leaving Nehru Park Wednesday morning."They showed me the first page of the FIR for a short while. It mentioned a post I had made on X on Aug 26 about SIR and elections in West Bengal. I was not shown the second page of the FIR; so, I am at the police headquarters with a letter from my lawyers to seek a copy, which they are required to provide to me," Joshi said.Police sources said as Joshi was not arrested and only questioned, there was no need to provide a copy of the FIR at this stage.Sources said that the cops questioned him regarding his post on X that called for "Nuremberg style trial" - military tribunals held after World War II - of the chief election commission in connection with the West Bengal elections while demanding that they be held again.During questioning, Joshi claimed, he was asked about his social media activity, including his post on the chief election commissioner and another he made on Aug 13.Earlier in the day, Joshi posted on X that he was not allowed to inform his family and friends that he was being questioned by police offi-cials Wednesday."Informing an individual's family during interrogation or detention is a legal mandate, not an optional courtesy... I was only permitted to make a call at 6.38pm, leaving my family & friends in total panic the entire day," he posted on X, tagging Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar.Delhi Police, however, rejected the allegations, asserting that all mandated legal provisions were followed during the questioning. Police said that following their request to join the investigation, Joshi came to the special cell's office in New Friends Colony in his own vehicle and was escorted home safely and cordially in the evening.Sources in Delhi Police had said Wednesday that Joshi and his wife were duly informed about the questioning and the registration of an FIR.
Article Summary: Ex-bureaucrat Ashish Joshi was questioned by Delhi Police's special cell for several hours Wednesday. Joshi, a 1992-batch officer of the Indian Post and Telecommunication Accounts and Finance Service, said he and his lawyers were yet to be pro-vided with a copy of the FIR.

Article Title: ‘World has reached the moon, we still carry children’: 80-year wait for bridge in Chhattisgarh's Sonpal village
Article Text:
In Sonpal village, daily life is disrupted by the absence of a crucial bridge





RAIPUR: “The world has reached the moon, but we still carry our children on our shoulders across the stream to help them reach school.” That is how residents of remote Sonpal village in Durgukondal block of Kanker district describe an eight-decade wait for a bridge they say has been promised by successive governments but never built.For villagers, the missing bridge is not merely an infrastructure gap. During the rains, it determines whether children can reach school, whether families can travel for work or treatment, and whether anyone can cross the village boundary without risking a fall into the swollen stream.Videos of parents carrying children on their shoulders through the flooded crossing have surfaced on social media, drawing attention to the village’s daily struggle.One of the women said villagers had even travelled to the state capital with applications seeking a bridge, but nothing changed. “It feels as if we are still not part of independent India,” she said.“The four months of monsoon are the worst. If someone falls ill, an ambulance cannot reach us. Children miss school, and sometimes their books get washed away in the water,” she said. “How are our children supposed to go to school? If they have to attend, the only option is for parents to carry them on their shoulders, otherwise their uniforms get soaked and covered in mud.They fall and others are so short, they can't stand in that water. Who would understand our pain? A bridge has to be built here.”Village head Sanuram Dugga said generations have lived with the same demand. “Our fathers and grandfathers kept asking for this bridge and died waiting. Now our generation is asking for it,” he said. “Governments come and go— everyone said it would be built. The promises were made, not the bridge.”A 2.3km blacktop road, constructed about three years ago at a cost of crores, exists on both sides of the stream. But in between, the road gets inundated during the monsoon.During the monsoon, villagers say adults wade across at considerable risk, while younger children are carried on shoulders or backs to get them safely to the other side.Women in the village — Iswanti Rana, Subhadra Patel, Sagro Bai Dugga, Basanti Kumeti and Somari Yadav — said they have heard the same assurance since they got married in Sonpal: “The bridge will be built this year.” Now, their children are bearing the brunt.Residents say the absence of a crossing affects not only schoolchildren but anyone needing to reach markets, hospitals, workplaces or government offices outside the village.Mahendra Singh Thakur, a sub-engineer with the Bridge Corporation in Kanker, told reporters that the Sonpal bridge has been included in the 2026-27 budget and that a fresh estimate will now be prepared and forwarded for further action.For Sonpal, however, an estimate is still not a bridge.
Article Summary: In Sonpal village, daily life is disrupted by the absence of a crucial bridge. During the rains, it determines whether children can reach school, whether families can travel for work or treatment, and whether anyone can cross the village boundary without risking a fall into the swollen stream.

Article Title: 6 drug traffickers held in Lucknow with narcotic medicines worth Rs 1 crore
Article Text:
The arrests were made on Friday at Kanhaiya Pharma in Transport Nagar, Lucknow.





LUCKNOW: The Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) operational unit in Lucknow has arrested six active drug traffickers and recovered a large consignment of narcotic and psychotropic medicines, including codeine-based cough syrup, tramadol capsules, and alprazolam tablets, collectively valued at an estimated Rs 1 crore.The arrests were made on Friday at Kanhaiya Pharma in Transport Nagar, Lucknow.Kishan Vaswani, Sameer Ahmed, Shad Irshad, Umesh Kumar, Satendra Singh, and Vishal Chaurasia were arrested.According to the ANTF, the accused were found in possession of 720 bottles of 100-ml ONEREX cough syrup containing codeine, 1,20,000 SPASMONAM PLUS capsules containing Tramadol Hydrochloride, and 9,60,000 ALZOMAC-0.5 tablets containing Alprazolam.Besides the drugs, the team also recovered seven mobile phones and Rs 11,140 in cash from the suspects.A case has been registered at Sarojini Nagar police station in the Lucknow Commissionerate under Sections 8, 21, 22, and 29 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act. Police said legal proceedings have been initiated against all six accused.During interrogation, the arrested suspects reportedly told investigators that they operated together to illegally procure and sell narcotic medicines for higher profits.They allegedly pooled money to purchase the medicines and subsequently delivered the consignments to different parties for monetary gain. The money earned from the transactions was then divided among the members of the group and used for their personal expenses and lifestyles, police said.Investigators said the questioning of the accused had yielded important information regarding the suspected drug network. The ANTF is now working on the forward and backward linkages of the case to identify the source from which the medicines were procured, the intended recipients of the consignment, and other persons associated with the network.Further investigation is underway to establish the complete supply chain and identify other individuals involved in the illegal trade.
Article Summary: The arrests were made on Friday at Kanhaiya Pharma in Transport Nagar, Lucknow. The suspects allegedly pooled money to purchase the medicines and delivered the consignments to different parties for monetary gain. The money earned from the transactions was then divided among the members of the group and used for their personal expenses.

Article Title: Konda Surekha tied rakhi to CM Revanth Reddy. Days later, he dropped her from his cabinet
Article Text:
Konda Surekha tied rakhi to CM Revanth Reddy

Controversy over daughter’s remarks

Surekha sacked from Cabinet





HYDERABAD: Days before minister Konda Surekha was sacked from the Cabinet, she was seen tying a rakhi to chief minister A Revanth Reddy at his residence, amid a controversy over remarks made by her daughter against the CM and the Congress party.In the video, Surekha, along with Women and Child Welfare Minister Seethakka, is seen tying a rakhi to Revanth Reddy during Raksha Bandhan celebrations.After the celebrations, Revanth posted on X: “On the occasion of Raksha Bandhan, which stands as a symbol of the bond between sisters and brothers, ministers Seethakka and Konda Surekha tied rakhis. I wish that this Raksha Bandhan festival brings joy to every girl child. #RakshaBandhan #Rakhi #Telangana.”In a separate post, he said: “To every elder sister, younger sister. People’s governance is Rakshabandhan. #RakshaBandhan #Rakhi #Telangana.”Speaking to reporters, Surekha said she had tied a rakhi to Revanth as she had done over the past two years.Asked about demands from Congress legislators for action against her, she said: “I do not want to comment on this auspicious festive day.”She added that she had prayed for the blessings of women to remain with Revanth.“Don’t single me out in this case. Today is a festival day and we all women have tied rakhis to the CM,” she said.The Raksha Bandhan celebrations came amid a controversy over remarks made by Surekha’s daughter, Konda Susmita, against Revanth and the Congress party.Susmita had criticised Revanth after he stated that sitting Parkal MLA Revuri Prakash Reddy would be given the Congress ticket from the constituency in the next Assembly election.A contender for the ticket herself, Susmita had said on August 19 that the CM did not have the authority to make such a decision and had also levelled other allegations against him.Surekha maintained that she could not be held responsible for her adult daughter’s comments. However, several Congress MLAs and MLCs demanded action against her.The TPCC disciplinary committee subsequently recommended action against Surekha for failing to condemn her daughter’s remarks.CM A Revanth Reddy later dropped Konda Surekha from his Cabinet, amid growing concerns over indiscipline within the state Congress.Sources told that the Congress high command had preferred Surekha to resign, but she refused to quit and travelled to Delhi to present her case before the party leadership.After meeting Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Surekha said she had explained her position and challenged the high command to take whatever action it deemed appropriate.She reiterated that her daughter was an adult and that her remarks should not be linked to her.Revanth had also taken up the matter with AICC general secretary (organisation) K C Venugopal in Delhi and sought action against Surekha. Venugopal’s refusal to meet Surekha had further fuelled speculation that disciplinary action was imminent.
Article Summary: Konda Surekha was seen tying a rakhi to chief minister A Revanth Reddy at his residence. The celebrations came amid a controversy over remarks made by her daughter, Konda Susmita, against Revanth and the Congress party.Surekha maintained that she could not be held responsible for her adult daughter's comments.

Article Title: A popular DM, a sudden exit, an unanswered question
Article Text:
Divya Mittal voluntarily resigned from the IAS after a thirteen-year career.

Why Her Exit Stunned Many

Popular, but sometimes at odds

From London to the IAS

Did she hit a plateau?

What comes next?





Today, I voluntarily resigned from the IAS, bringing an unforgettable 13-year journey to a close.” With those words, Divya Mittal announced on social media on Sunday that she was walking away from the civil services. The resignation of the 43-year-old, 2013-batch Uttar Pradesh-cadre officer, who was serving as special secretary in the revenue department, is yet to be formally accepted.Mittal has not disclosed why she quit, telling TOI that she will reveal her plans at the appropriate time. Her farewell post instead retraced her journey from IIT-Delhi and IIM-Bangalore to a job in London, and then back to India to repay what she called a “debt to this soil”.Her decision surprised colleagues and admirers because Mittal had acquired a public following unusual for a bureaucrat. In Mirzapur and Deoria, she became known as an accessible, hands-on administrator who used social media to communicate her work.Her best-known initiative brought piped water to Lahuriya Deh, a remote hilltop hamlet whose residents had long depended on tankers and water collected from pits.In her farewell note, Mittal recalled an elderly woman silently touching her head and blessing her when water reached the village.Village representatives also remember “Mera Gaon, Mera Gaurav”, a WhatsApp group connecting more than 800 pradhans with district officials. Mittal would tag officials when problems were raised and monitor the response, effectively giving village heads a direct line to the administration.Those who worked with her describe two distinct sides to her administrative personality. She was soft-spoken and approachable with members of the public, but could lose her temper in official meetings when instructions were ignored. Her willingness to take decisions independently won her admirers, but it did not always make for easy relations with elected representatives.The completion of the Lahuriya Deh water project itself became a source of friction. Mittal performed the “jal puja” when water reached the village, but elected representatives were absent. Critics accused her of sidelining politicians; her supporters saw an administrator more interested in finishing the work than managing political optics.She was transferred from Mirzapur soon after the event and remained without a posting for several months.There had been confrontations earlier, too. During her tenure as Sant Kabir Nagar DM, Mittal found herself at odds with then district minister-in-charge Ashish Patel, husband of Union minister and Mirzapur MP Anupriya Patel, after she sent a representative to receive him instead of attending personally. As Deoria DM, differences during a District Development Coordination and Monitoring Committee meeting also generated controversy.Her visibility added another layer to the friction. In Deoria, she came to be known as the “reel wali DM” due to her frequent social-media posts on govt initiatives, community events and public outreach. Supporters saw it as an effort to make the administration more accessible. Detractors questioned whether the officer’s public profile was beginning to overshadow the institution she represented.Such attention was far removed from the circumstances in which Mittal grew up. Born in Rewari, Haryana, she was raised in a modest household before her family moved to Delhi, which is listed as her home district in civil-service records.She studied engineering at IIT-Delhi between 2001 and 2005 and then attended IIM-Bangalore. After completing her management degree, she joined JPMorgan in London.Her husband, Gagandeep Singh Dhillon, had travelled much the same route a few years before her. He was Mittal’s senior at both IIT-Delhi and IIM-Bangalore and subsequently worked with Citigroup in London. The couple married in April 2007 and began their corporate careers in the UK.Despite well-paying jobs in international finance, they jointly decided to return to India in 2009 and prepare for the civil services. Mittal eventually joined the IAS in 2013. Dhillon entered the Indian Trade Service in 2011 and worked in areas including foreign trade and export controls.The parallel between their careers did not end there. In May 2022, Dhillon resigned from govt service and returned to financial markets. He now works as an algorithmic trader at Neuracap, according to his LinkedIn profile. Four years later, Mittal has followed him out of the civil services, although she has given no indication that she intends to return to finance.Former colleagues say Mittal’s ambition and appetite for difficult assignments were evident early in her career. Her batchmate Sunil Kumar Verma recalls that when delays arose in cadre allocation at the Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration, Mittal and two other officers took on the technically demanding exercise themselves and completed it for the entire batch.Some senior officers who know her describe Mittal as an “over-achiever” and believe professional stagnation may have influenced her move. Having moved rapidly from elite academic institutions and international finance to demanding district assignments, she may have found the slower phases of a bureaucratic career frustrating, they say.Her transfer from Mirzapur, extended wait for another posting, and eventual move from Deoria DM to special secretary in revenue department form part of that reading. But it’s just that: an interpretation offered by colleagues, not an explanation confirmed by Mittal.She has said her resignation was neither impulsive nor due to pressure.Her interests outside administration offer some clues, though not necessarily an answer. Mittal is the author of, “The Crafted Genius”, a book about preparation, discipline and resilience. Her social-media posts frequently discuss parenting, while her writing has examined what formal education fails to teach — emotional regulation, communication, financial management, loneliness and mental health.Mittal has indicated that writing, teaching and social service could be among the avenues she explores next.Politics is another possibility being discussed, particularly in Mirzapur, where her resignation has revived memories of her tenure. Abhinav Tripathi, pradhan of Dhawespur Kakrahi, says he would like Mittal to contest an election from the district and would contribute to her campaign if she did.The proximity of the 2027 UP assembly polls has inevitably added to that speculation. Mittal, however, has said nothing to suggest that a political debut is imminent.Her farewell note offers only one certainty: she may have surrendered the office through which she pursued her idea of public service, but she does not see herself as having surrendered the idea itself.“The position may be gone,” she wrote, “but the dream this country’s soil gave me will not leave me.”
Article Summary: Divya Mittal announced on social media that she was walking away from the civil services. The 43-year-old, 2013-batch Uttar Pradesh-cadre officer was serving as special secretary in the revenue department. Mittal has not disclosed why she quit, telling TOI that she will reveal her plans at the appropriate time.

Article Title: ‘No inconvenience to devotees’: CM Yogi Adityanath pitches grand temple complexes in Mathura-Vrindavan
Article Text:
CM Yogi Adityanath also visited the Yogmaya temple, Keshavdev temple and Bhagwat Bhavan.





MATHURA: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Friday said the state government plans to develop grand temple complexes in Mathura-Vrindavan on the lines of those in Ayodhya and Kashi.The statement by the chief minister came on the second day of his visit to Mathura. He arrived at the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Temple on Friday morning on the occasion of Shri Krishna Janmashtami.The chief minister first performed ritual worship of cows in the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi complex. Following the gau pujan, Adityanath offered special prayers and sought blessings from ‘Lala’ (Lord Krishna), who is enshrined in the main sanctum sanctorum.After offering prayers in the main sanctum, Adityanath also visited the Yogmaya Temple, Keshavdev Temple and Bhagwat Bhavan, located within the complex.Speaking to the press after his visit, the CM said, "Today, you will not even be able to find invaders. They have all disappeared. A grand temple of Lord Ram has been built in Ayodhya. One of the world’s largest temples has come up in Ayodhya. Those who do not like all this are trying to defame Ayodhya.After a wait of 500 years, that work has finally been accomplished... Keeping in mind the spiritual and cultural significance of this Braj region, the Braj Teerth Vikas Parishad, along with public representatives, is working to develop it in a manner befitting its importance and to provide better facilities for devotees. Our effort is to create a similar devotee-friendly environment and infrastructure in Mathura and Vrindavan as has been developed in Ayodhya and Kashi, so that no devotee faces any inconvenience and there is no obstacle or threat to their faith."Taking a swipe at political opponents, Adityanath said his government believed in “Krishna Kanhaiya, Lord Ram, Baba Vishwanath and Maa Vindhyavasini” and respected the faith of the people.“But can those whose faith lies in Babur and Aurangzeb respect your faith?” he asked, accusing the “followers of Babur and Aurangzeb” of attempting to create divisions in society.Adityanath alleged that such forces wanted to weaken social harmony, compromise security, play with the future of young people and threaten the safety of women. He said the BJP’s “double-engine government” would not allow such designs to succeed.The chief minister also contrasted the present government’s approach with that of previous administrations, claiming that earlier governments avoided visiting such places because of “vote-bank concerns”.Referring to the changing identity of the Braj region, Adityanath said it was now being associated with religious and cultural celebrations, including Rangotsav, Braj Raj Utsav and Vaishnav Kumbh, rather than incidents of violence and disorder.Extending Janmashtami greetings to people across Uttar Pradesh, Adityanath called upon citizens to remain committed to their duties towards the country, society, Sanatan Dharma and their families.“If everyone fulfils their responsibilities honestly, it will not take long for India to become a developed nation and Uttar Pradesh a developed state,” he said.Notably, this is not the first time that the CM has spoken about developing temple complexes in Mathura on the lines of those in Ayodhya and Varanasi. He has repeatedly linked Mathura-Vrindavan’s religious development with the transformation of Ayodhya and Kashi, including in 2021-22 when he spoke about Mathura and Vrindavan after the Ram Temple and Kashi Vishwanath projects."There were numerous invasions, and many attempted to impose their own faiths upon India, yet no one could erase Sanatan Dharma. Those who had the audacity to try and obliterate Sanatan Dharma were themselves reduced to dust and faded into oblivion. However, not only in Braj Bhoomi but across all of India, the memory of Shri Krishna and Radha Rani serves as an inspiration for us today and fosters an atmosphere of enthusiasm and progress for future generations," Yogi Adityanath said.Janmashtami, also known as Krishna Janmashtami or Gokulashtami, is observed to mark the birth of Lord Krishna, regarded as the eighth avatar of Lord Vishnu.The festival is observed on the eighth day, or Ashtami, of the Krishna Paksha in the month of Bhadrapada, according to the Hindu lunisolar calendar.
Article Summary: Chief minister Yogi Adityanath visited the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Temple in Mathura. He also visited the Yogmaya Temple, Keshavdev Temple and Bhagwat Bhavan. He said his government believed in “Krishna Kanhaiya, Lord Ram, Baba Vishwanath and Maa Vindhyavasini’

Article Title: Apple follows Google Maps, renames Lake Ontario to Lake America; US President calls change of names 'complete, ratified, and binding'
Article Text:
Apple follows Google Maps with Lake America name change

Apple follows Google Maps with Lake America change

Canada continues to call it Lake Ontario

MapQuest refuses to rename the lake

After Google Maps, Apple Maps has now renamed Lake Ontario as “Lake America” for users in the US after a presidential executive order. The update means Apple users in the United States will see ‘Lake America’ when viewing the Great Lake that sits between New York and Canada’s Ontario province. Users outside the US will continue to see the lake as Lake Ontario. Sharing a post on X (formerly Twitter), US President Donald Trump called the name change 'complete, ratified, and binding'.“Apple Maps has just announced that it has changed the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America, so now that very important change of names, between Google Maps and Apple Maps, is complete, ratified, and binding. Thank you for your attention to this matter! President DONALD J. TRUMP,” Trump wrote in the post.Google Maps changed its display label for Lake Ontario over the weekend, saying it was following the US Geographic Names Information System (GNIS), which had formally changed the name in the United States. Google then said its Maps service would show different names depending on the user’s location. People in the US would see “Lake America”, users in Canada would see “Lake Ontario”, while users outside the US and Canada would see both names.Canadian officials have rejected the name change and said the country will continue using Lake Ontario in its official records. Prime Minister Mark Carney has pointed to the history of the name, saying it is more than 400 years old and comes from the Wendat word Ontari’io.“The name is more than 400 years old, predating both the Confederation of Canada and the Declaration of Independence of the United States of America,” Carney said.Notably, not every mapping service has followed Google and Apple. MapQuest has rejected the request to use “Lake America”. The company posted a screenshot showing the name Lake Ontario with the message: “We’re not changing it.” According to a Guardian report, the move reportedly helped MapQuest rise to the top of Apple’s US App Store rankings.
Article Summary: Apple follows Google Maps with Lake America name change. Users in the US will see ‘Lake America’ when viewing the Great Lake. Users outside the US and Canada will continue to see the lake as Lake Ontario. Canadian officials have rejected the name change and said the country will continue using Lake Ontario in its official records.

Article Title: Property dealer murder: Kin stage protest
Article Text:
New Delhi:





Family members of 42-year-old property dealer Pramod Dahiya, who was shot dead outside a gym in Narela on Thursday, staged a sit-in and blocked the road on Friday.Around 12.30 pm, Dahiya’s family members, along with acquaintances and hundreds of people from Nahri village, gathered on the Narela-Lampur Road to protest the killing. The protesters agreed to clear the road and restore traffic following an appeal by police.Sources said the suspects appeared to be between 20 and 25 years old.A social media post, purportedly issued by the Himanshu Bhau gang, claimed responsibility for the killing. The post, which named Himanshu Bhau and Neeraj Faridpur, claimed that Dahiya had earlier been warned on the phone but he “thought that having a licensed weapon would save his life.”Preliminary inquiry revealed that Dahiya’s business partner had allegedly received an extortion demand of Rs 2 crore. A case in connection with the alleged demand had already been registered in Sonipat, police said.
Article Summary: Pramod Dahiya, 42, was shot dead outside a gym in Narela on Thursday. A social media post, purportedly issued by the Himanshu Bhau gang, claimed responsibility for the killing. The protesters agreed to clear the road and restore traffic following an appeal by police.

Article Title: ‘Treatment not denied’: Court rejects interim bail plea in hotel fire case
Article Text: New Delhi: A court has dismissed the interim bail plea of Flourish Stay owner Lokesh Bajaj, accused in the June 3 Malviya Nagar hotel fire that claimed 23 lives. The court rejected Bajaj’s plea for four weeks’ bail on the ground of his deteriorating health.Principal district and sessions judge Samar Vishal said there was no material indicating any inadequacy or denial of medical treatment, and noted that Bajaj was shifted from Deen Dayal Upadhyay Hospital to Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital when his condition worsened.Bajaj was diagnosed with intestinal obstruction and doctors advised surgery. His family sought his release to get an independent opinion from his own doctor and, if required, have him treated at a private hospital.However, the court noted that Bajaj had already “undergone the requisite surgical intervention” at RML and the procedure was “uneventful”.
Article Summary: Lokesh Bajaj is accused in the June 3 Malviya Nagar hotel fire that claimed 23 lives. The court rejected his plea for four weeks’ bail on the ground of his deteriorating health. The family sought his release to get an independent opinion from his own doctor and have him treated at a private hospital.

Article Title: Traffic crawls, people wade as rain turns roads into waterways
Article Text:
New Delhi:





Several roads near the airport, AIIMS , Connaught Place and Anand Vihar were inundated Friday, forcing many to wade through flooded stretches and traffic to crawl at several key points.The downpour once again exposed the capital’s drainage woes, with the airport corridor being among the worst affected stretches. Waterlogging was reported at Terminal 3 underpass, an important access route for airport-bound traffic, with visuals showing a bus stranded inside the inundated tunnel. Water quickly choked surrounding roads as vehicles were forced to slow down or take diversions.South Delhi also had its share of trouble. Roads around AIIMS, Mahipalpur and Basant Gaon were waterlogged, while Subroto Park saw large stretches submerged. Visuals showed water flowing down from the flyover onto the already inundated road, making conditions more challenging for motorists.Waterlogging was also reported in Mundka, Public Works Department (PWD) sources said, adding that inputs were being forwarded to designated authorities for necessary action.Central Delhi was no better. Parts of Connaught Place, including its outer circle, were waterlogged, while Akbar Road was flooded.New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) data listed Kidwai Nagar East, Janpath Lane, Sarojini Nagar and Tansen Marg among other waterlogged locations. D-Block Sector-8, Dwarka, which falls under the jurisdiction of Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), was waterlogged too.In east Delhi, areas near Anand Vihar Metro Station were under water, inconveniencing commuters. Near Moti Bagh Metro Station, a sizeable portion of the road was flooded, while waterlogging was also reported near Hanuman Mandir close to ISBT.Traffic congestion was reported around Subroto Park and Connaught Place, while the Mahipalpur-Gurgaon stretch, including the flyover and toll plaza area, also witnessed traffic crawling.Commuters took to social media to flag the ordeal. A person posted, “Massive traffic jam on flyovers to airport. Many passengers are likely to miss their flights. What kind of traffic management is this? People are stuck for 45 minutes.”Neither PWD nor NDMC provided an official response about the waterlogging and traffic disruption. Sources in the traffic police department said the situation on stretches to the airport, including T3 access road, was cleared within 15 minutes. They added that traffic officials were deployed on the ground at other affected locations as well.Delhi Pradesh Congress Committee president Devender Yadav said despite chief minister’s assurance that desilting and cleaning of drainage systems would reduce waterlogging, the rain created tremendous inconvenience to the public.
Article Summary: Several roads near the airport, AIIMS, Connaught Place and Anand Vihar were inundated Friday, forcing many to wade through flooded stretches. Waterlogging was reported at Terminal 3 underpass, an important access route for airport- bound traffic. South Delhi also had its share of trouble.

Article Title: $25,000 cash stolen from women’s checked-in bag on Mumbai-Dubai flight
Article Text:
Thane women lose $25,000 cash from checked-in baggage on Dubai flight (AI image used for representational purpose only)





MUMBAI: A $25,000 (over Rs 23.6 lakh) cash theft from the checked-in baggage of two Thane homemakers is the biggest of 16 baggage theft cases registered at Sahar police station between Jan and Aug this year. None of the cases has been solved.The latest FIR was registered on Sept 3 after the two family friends, aged 40 and 46, alleged that their cash was stolen during their Aug 26 Mumbai-Dubai journey. They had boarded a SpiceJet flight from Mumbai and discovered after landing in Dubai that one bag had been broken open and the cash was missing.The women spent four days in their hotel room without money before returning to Mumbai on Sunday. The 40-year-old woman has urged police to examine the attendance records of loaders assigned to their flight between 11am and 2pm on Aug 26.She suspects that someone who saw the cash during X-ray screening may have alerted a loader. According to her, police said hundreds of loaders were on duty and CCTV cameras did not cover some stretches between the conveyor belt and the aircraft cargo hold. The women were also told they should not have carried cash in checked-in baggage.The family had taken a loan and carried its savings to Dubai to shop for a wedding scheduled in Dec and meet travel expenses. "I will pursue the matter until the money is recovered," she said.The second-biggest case was registered on April 24 after Borivli resident Vandana Bhise (48), a senior executive at a private firm, reported losing six gold-studded rings worth Rs 15 lakh while returning from Chicago to Mumbai.In two cases on Aug 26 and 27, MBBS students from Ratnagiri and Sambhaji Nagar reported losses of Rs 4.5 lakh and Rs 2 lakh respectively after finding their bag locks broken on arrival in Moscow. They had travelled from Mumbai on Egypt Air and Etihad flights.Other complainants included seamen, a businesswoman and a senior executive who reported losing gold ornaments, mobile phones, cash or entire bags.DCP (West Zone-1) Nimit Goyal said he would verify the case details before commenting.Former Mumbai police commissioner D Sivanandhan said local police should develop an informer network inside the airport instead of relying on CCTV footage. He said crime branch should investigate the cases, alleging that thieves could exploit CCTV blind spots and be alerted after valuables were spotted during X-ray screening.
Article Summary: Thane women lose $25,000 cash from checked-in baggage on Dubai flight. It is the biggest of 16 baggage theft cases registered at Sahar police station between Jan and Aug this year. None of the cases has been solved.

Article Title: BMC removes 38 illegal stalls in Andheri West under ‘Pedestrian First’ campaign
Article Text:
The opposition parties in the BMC demanded that the proposal be sent back to the administration for reconsideration

Mumbai:





The BMC removed 38 unauthorized stalls in the Andheri (West) area as part of its ongoing ‘Pedestrian First’ campaign.The action was carried out at Andheri (West) railway station, Vile Parle (West) railway station, Jogeshwari (West) railway station, Veera Desai Marg and Swami Vivekanand Marg. In the first phase of the campaign, encroachments are being removed from 200 footpaths across Mumbai. Large-scale action under the K-West Ward office has been underway since last week.The ‘Pedestrian First’ campaign has been undertaken to make footpaths in Mumbai available for pedestrians. Accordingly, encroachments will be removed on 27 roads in the Vile Parle area. Emphasis has been laid on making obstruction-free the footpaths in areas with heavy pedestrian movement on Swami Vivekanand Marg. In the first phase, encroachments on six footpaths were removed in the Andheri (West) station area, Vile Parle (West) station area, Jogeshwari station area, Ram Ganesh Gadkari Marg, Veera Desai Marg and Swami Vivekanand Marg.The BMC said the drive has cleared pedestrian passage at Andheri West station, Vile Parle West station, Jogeshwari station and Swami Vivekanand Marg. According to the civic body, the clearance is expected to help reduce vehicular and pedestrian congestion during peak hours and provide obstruction-free pedestrian access towards Swami Vivekanand Marg.
Article Summary: BMC removed 38 unauthorized stalls in the Andheri (West) area as part of its ongoing ‘Pedestrian First’ campaign. In the first phase of the campaign, encroachments are being removed from 200 footpaths across Mumbai.
